items.title: Wrongful Accusation Completed, and Wrongful Teaching's Six Ways to Fail

items.zh: 言引無義故，名非義語者。言麁獷故，名非法語者。言挾瞋恚故，名非靜語者。又於邪說法時，不正思審而宣說故，名不思量語。為勝聽者而宣說故，名不靜語。
items.en: Because the words serve no genuine purpose, this is called pointless speech. Because the words are harsh, this is called improper speech. Because the words carry hatred, this is called agitated speech. Further, when teaching the Dharma improperly: because the teaching is delivered without careful, sound reflection beforehand, this is called unconsidered speech. Because it is delivered chiefly to impress an especially eminent listener, this is called restless speech.

items.zh: 非時而說，前後義趣不相屬故，名雜亂語。不中理因而宣說故，名非有教語。引不相應為譬況故，名非有喻語。顯穢染故，名非有法語。
items.en: Because it is delivered at the wrong time, its content disconnected front to back, this is called disordered speech. Because the reasoning offered does not actually hold up, this is called speech without genuine doctrinal grounding. Because the analogy drawn does not actually fit, this is called speech without a genuine example. Because it displays defilement rather than dispelling it, this is called speech without any real Dharma in it at all.

items.title: Idle Chatter During Entertainment, Frivolous Speech Closes, and Covetousness Opens

items.zh: 又於歌笑嬉戲等時，及觀舞樂、戲笑、俳說等時，有引無義語。此中略義者，謂顯如前說三時綺語。
items.en: Further, during singing, laughter, and play, and while watching dance, music, comic performance, and theatre, there arises speech that serves no genuine purpose. The brief meaning here shows that frivolous speech, as already explained, occurs across these three settings.

items.zh: 復次，諸貪欲者者，此是總句。由猛利貪者，謂於他所有，由貪增上，欲為己有，起決定執故。於財者，謂世俗財類。具者，謂所受用資具。即此二種總名為物。凡彼所有定當屬我者，此顯貪欲生起行相。
items.en: Further, "those who covet" is the summary phrase. "Through intense craving" means holding a settled, determined conviction, driven by overwhelming desire, to make what belongs to another one's own. "Wealth" refers to ordinary worldly riches. "Goods" refers to the requisites one actually makes use of — these two together are simply called "possessions." "Whatever they have should rightly belong to me" shows the very mode in which covetousness actually arises in the mind.

items.zh: 此中略義者，當知顯示貪欲自性、貪欲所緣、貪欲行相。

items.title: Ill Will Completed: Wishing Harm, Loss, and Grief Upon Another

items.zh: 復次，瞋恚心者者，此是總句。惡意分別者，謂於他有情所，由瞋恚增上力，欲為損害，起決定執故。當殺者，謂欲傷害其身。當害者，謂欲損惱其身。
items.en: Further, "one with a mind of ill will" is the summary phrase. "Malicious intent" means holding a settled, determined conviction, driven by overwhelming hatred, to bring harm upon another sentient being. "Wishing to kill" means wishing to injure their very body. "Wishing to harm" means wishing to cause their body distress.

items.zh: 當為衰損者，謂欲令彼財物損耗。彼當自獲種種憂惱者，謂欲令彼自失財物。此中略義，如前應知。
items.en: "Wishing for their ruin" means wishing to see their wealth wasted and destroyed. "Wishing they themselves come to endure every kind of grief" means wishing to see them lose their own possessions. The brief meaning here should be understood exactly as with covetousness above.

items.title: Wrong View Opens: From Private Conviction to Public Doctrine

items.zh: 復次，諸邪見者者，此是總句。起如是見者，此顯自心忍可欲樂當所說義。立如是論者，此顯授他當所說義。
items.en: Further, "those who hold wrong views" is the summary phrase. "Giving rise to such a view" shows one's own mind assenting to and taking pleasure in a position not yet spoken aloud. "Establishing such a doctrine" shows that same position now being actively taught and transmitted to others.

items.zh: 無有施與、無有愛養、無有祠祀者，謂由三種意樂非撥施故。一、財物意樂，二、清淨意樂，三、祀天意樂。供養火天，名為祠祀。
items.en: "There is no giving, no caring for elders, no offerings" arises from three underlying attitudes that together deny the value of giving: attachment to one's own wealth, a mistaken sense that meditative purity alone suffices, and devotion solely to fire-worship. "Offerings" here specifically means veneration paid to the fire deity.

items.zh: 又顯非撥戒修所生善能治所治故，及顯非撥施所生善能治所治故，說如是言：無有妙行，無有惡行。又顯非撥此三種善能治所治所得果故，說如是言：無有妙行、惡行二業果及異熟。
items.en: Further, denying that the wholesome states produced by moral discipline and meditation can actually counter what they are meant to counter, and denying the same for generosity, one says: "there is no good conduct, no bad conduct." Further, denying that these three wholesome practices produce any actual result at all, one says: "neither good nor bad conduct has any karmic fruit or ripening."

items.title: Denying This World and the Next, and Denying Parents and Spontaneous Rebirth

items.zh: 又顯非撥流轉依處緣故，說如是言：無有此世，無有他世。又顯非撥彼所託緣故，及非撥彼種子緣故，說如是言：無母無父。又顯非撥流轉士夫故，說如是言：無有化生有情。
items.en: Further, denying the very basis on which beings circulate through rebirth, one says: "there is no this-world, no other-world." Further, denying both the condition a being relies on for conception and the seed-condition it depends on, one says: "there is no mother, no father." Further, denying the being that actually carries a life's continuity forward, one says: "there is no spontaneously arising being."

items.title: Denying the True Arhat, and Ten Marks of What Genuine Attainment Actually Is

items.zh: 又顯非撥流轉對治還滅故，說如是言：世間無有真阿羅漢，乃至廣說。已趣各別煩惱寂靜，故名正至。於諸有情遠離邪行，行無倒行，故名正行。因時，名此世間。果時，名彼世間。
items.en: Further, denying that there is any genuine antidote or cessation of the round of rebirth, one says: "there is no true arhat in the world" — stated in full detail. "Having genuinely reached the stilling of every distinct affliction" is called correctly arriving. "Towards all beings, being free of wrongful conduct, acting only in accordance with what is true" is called correct conduct. The time of practising the cause is called "this side"; the time of realising the result is called "the far side."

items.zh: 自士夫力之所作故，名為自然。通慧者，謂第六。已證者，謂由見道。具足者，謂由修道。顯示者，自所知故，為他說故。我生已盡等，當知如餘處分別。
items.en: "Accomplished purely through one's own effort" is called self-attained. "Transcendent wisdom" refers to the sixth of the six superknowledges, the knowledge of the exhaustion of defilement. "Already realised" refers to what is attained through the path of seeing. "Fully complete" refers to what is attained through the path of cultivation. "Self-demonstrated" means knowing it for oneself and being able to teach it to others. "My rebirth is exhausted" and the rest should be understood as explained elsewhere.

items.title: Four Kinds of Denial, and the "By Person" Classification Closes Entirely

items.zh: 此中略義者，謂顯示謗因、謗果、誹謗功用、謗真實事。功用者，謂殖種功用、任持功用，來往功用、感生業功用。
items.en: The brief meaning here shows: denial of cause, denial of result, denial of causal function, and denial of what is genuinely real. "Function" refers to the function of planting a seed, the function of sustaining what has been conceived, the function of coming and going between lives, and the function of actually generating a new rebirth.

items.zh: 又有略義差別。謂顯示誹謗若因、若果、若流轉緣、若流轉士夫，及顯誹謗彼對治還滅。

items.title: Two Careful Distinctions Close the Unwholesome Side, and the Wholesome Side Opens

items.zh: 又誹謗流轉者，應知謗因，不謗自相。謗還滅者，應知謗彼功德，不謗補特伽羅。復次，白品一切，翻前應知。
items.en: Further, one who denies the round of rebirth should be understood to deny only its cause, not the basic fact of beings' own transmigration. One who denies liberation should be understood to deny only its actual qualities, not the existence of the person who has attained it. Further, the wholesome side is, in every respect, simply the reverse of what has just been described.

items.zh: 謂翻欲邪行中，諸梵行者者，此是總句。當知此由三種清淨而得清淨。一、時分清淨，二、他信清淨，三、正行清淨。盡壽行故、久遠行故者，此顯時分清淨。
items.en: Reversing sexual misconduct: "those who practice celibacy" is the summary phrase. It should be understood that this purity is achieved through three kinds of purity: purity of duration, purity of others' trust, and purity of correct conduct. "Practised for one's entire life" and "practised across a vast span of time" show purity of duration.

items.zh: 諍處雪故名清，無違越故名淨，此二總顯他信清淨。此中或有清而非淨，應作四句。初句者，謂實毀犯，於諍得勝。第二句者，謂實不犯，於諍墮負。第三句者，謂實不犯，於諍得勝。第四句者，謂實毀犯，於諍墮負。
items.en: Being cleared when accused is called "clear"; not actually having transgressed is called "pure" — these two together constitute purity of others' trust. Here, one may be clear without being pure, and so four cases should be distinguished. In the first case, one has genuinely transgressed, yet prevails in the dispute. In the second, one has genuinely not transgressed, yet loses the dispute. In the third, one has genuinely not transgressed, and prevails in the dispute. In the fourth, one has genuinely transgressed, and loses the dispute.

blocks.text: Today completes the ten unwholesome courses with frivolous speech and the three mental courses: covetousness, ill will, and wrong view. The three mental courses are especially important in Yogācāra, which locates karma first in volition. Then the wholesome side begins.

Frivolous speech includes wrongful accusation, improper teaching of the Dharma, and idle talk during entertainment. Improper teaching fails in six ways; one is restless speech "to impress an especially eminent listener". Master Cháng Bǎi gives two readings: when eminent elders are present and the teacher grows unsettled, or when the teacher speaks to outdo the listeners out of conceit.

How broad is frivolous speech? Master Cháng Bǎi: "Apart from what is needed to communicate in daily life, any speech that brings no benefit is frivolous." He notes that the eight precepts include abstaining from watching song and dance. Most of our speech falls under this heading, which is why it is listed among the ten.
**Covetousness** (貪欲) is the wish to take what belongs to another: "May what is his become mine." It is a course of action even though it never leaves the mind.
**Ill will** (瞋恚) is "wishing harm, loss, and grief upon another". Again, mental only, and still karma.

**Wrong view** (邪見) denies cause and effect. The treatise distinguishes "giving rise to such a view" (private conviction) from "establishing such a doctrine" (teaching it publicly). Master Cháng Bǎi: "Giving rise to the view is inner thought; establishing the doctrine is already voicing it." On Day 59 the formal definition will show that wrong view is complete as mental karma once one has settled on denial.

It denies giving and offering, good and bad deeds and their results, this world and the next, parents, spontaneously born beings, and true arhats. Master Cháng Bǎi explains the "function" it denies: "Planting is the father, sustaining the mother, coming and going this world and the next, generating rebirth the spontaneously born being." Wrong view, then, denies the whole moral structure of life.

Denying the true arhat, the treatise adds ten marks of what genuine attainment is: one has truly cut off the afflictions, truly understood, and so on. The nihilist of Day 49 had only met counterfeits.
Wrong view denies in four ways: denying causes, results, functions, and what is real. With this, the portrait "by the person" is complete.

Two careful distinctions close the unwholesome side. Then the treatise turns to the ten wholesome courses, described by the same method. Master Cháng Bǎi's comment on one distinction, about whether a monastic accused of an offence is "clear" and "pure" in others' eyes: the worst case is "clear but not pure", winning the dispute while actually having transgressed. Appearing innocent matters less than being so.

quiz.q: The text lists five improper accusations. Conversely, what must a proper accusation have?
options: timely, true, beneficial, gentle, and calm — the right time, factual, for the other's benefit, soft-spoken, compassionate
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "The sūtras say the accuser needs five virtues: timely, true, beneficial, proper, and calm speech"; "the right time, for the other's benefit, factual without excess, gentle words, with compassion." Venerable Miào Jìng: exposing faults so they can be confessed is good-hearted; done wrongly, it becomes frivolous speech.

quiz.q: Improper Dharma teaching "for a 勝 listener" is called restless speech, rendered "to impress an especially eminent listener." What two readings of 勝 does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: (1) adjective: eminent elders are present and the speaker grows unsettled; (2) verb: speaking to outdo the listeners, with conceit
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "When eminent elders are in the audience and the speaker's mind is unsettled, that speech is restless"; "taking 勝 as a verb: to outdo the listeners, with the affliction of conceit." The translation takes the first. Venerable Miào Jìng: a wavering mind while teaching makes speech "restless."

quiz.q: The text says idle words arise during song, play, and entertainment. How broad does Master Cháng Bǎi say frivolous speech is?
options: apart from necessary communication, any speech not bringing benefit is frivolous — the eight precepts include not watching song and dance
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Apart from what's needed to communicate in daily life, any speech that brings no benefit is frivolous"; "the eight precepts include not watching song, dance, or shows." Venerable Miào Jìng: "By Buddhist standards, theatre and such all count as frivolous speech."

quiz.q: How do "giving rise to such a view" and "establishing such a doctrine" differ? The reading note says wrong view isn't complete as karma until taught. What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: the view is inner thought, the doctrine its public expression; wrong view is complete as mental karma once the resolve to deny is settled — teaching isn't required
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Giving rise to the view is inner thought; establishing the doctrine is already voicing it." §51 defines wrong view as "the desire to deny … determined resolve … and whatever mental action completes it" — complete as mental karma. The reading note's claim that it must be taught contradicts both the lecture and the note's own §51 (logged in the correction list).

quiz.q: The text says wrong view denies "function": planting, sustaining, coming and going, generating rebirth. How does Master Cháng Bǎi match them?
options: planting is the father, sustaining the mother, coming and going this and other worlds, generating rebirth the spontaneously born being (intermediate state)
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Planting is the father, sustaining the mother, coming and going this world and the next, generating rebirth the spontaneously born being." Venerable Miào Jìng agrees. Wrong view's summary: denying cause, result, function, and the real.

quiz.q: Purity of others' trust has four cases of "clear" and "pure." Which does Master Cháng Bǎi call worst?
options: clear but not pure — winning the dispute while actually having transgressed
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Worst is clear but not pure — winning the argument while actually having broken the precept." The four: guilty but cleared, innocent but losing, innocent and cleared, guilty and losing. Venerable Miào Jìng: the third is best; he also tells of a pratyekabuddha falsely accused who didn't defend himself.
